update.title: Added priority-based window pinning to Wayfire
update.summary: Built a Wayfire plugin that moved matched windows into a priority-ordered topmost scene, restored them when unpinned, and exposed configuration and IPC control.

preview.description: Namespace rules and IPC pinning feeding a priority-ordered Wayfire scene stack.

blocks.body:
## Pin windows at the scene boundary

I built Topmost Scene to keep selected Wayfire views above ordinary windows, drag overlays, and compositor effects. Configuration matched app IDs and namespaces automatically, while IPC pinned a specific view on demand.

Each pinned view carried a numeric priority. Reapplying the layer sorted those values before moving the existing scene nodes to the front of Wayfire’s root scene, so the order came from explicit data rather than focus timing or caller order.

blocks.code:
flowchart TD
  View[Wayfire view] --> Match{Configured namespace or IPC pin?}
  Match -->|Yes| Preserve[Preserve original parent]
  Preserve --> Topmost[Move to topmost scene]
  Priority[Configured priority] --> Topmost
  Topmost --> Restore[Restore on unpin or shutdown]
blocks.description: Pinning remained reversible because the plugin retained each view’s original scene parent.

blocks.body:
## Return views without recreating them

Before moving a view into the root scene, the plugin saved its original scene parent. When no pin rule remained, unpinning reattached the existing node to that parent. Disabling or unloading the plugin restored all tracked views, while view destruction removed their bookkeeping.

Moving and restoring the same node preserved the compositor object, input routing, and application lifecycle instead of creating a second representation of the window.

## Control the layer at runtime

Topmost Scene exposed `pin`, `unpin`, `list`, and `reapply` through IPC, while namespace and priority settings supplied persistent rules. A smaller Layer Stacker companion handled compatibility cases inside an existing layer, re-raising matched views after mapping, focus requests, or geometry changes.
